decision.reasoning: None of the three underwater employees show evidence of the scope, seniority, or organizational irreplaceability that would justify a "critical retain" flag. Evaluating each: - NYX-001 (L6, compa-ratio 0.43): Despite the L6 level and largest compa-ratio gap, the role summary describes a new-grad IC working under supervision on a single sub-block (CDC synchronizer, register-map RTL) of one PHY controller, with one tapeout to their name, no direct reports, and scope explicitly "limited to a single sub-block." This reads as an early-career/junior profile (the L6 label alone isn't sufficient evidence of seniority absent scope to match) with no indication of unique institutional knowledge, leadership, or broad technical authority. Losing this person would be a normal backfillable loss, not a critical one. - NYX-007 (L3, compa-ratio 0.76): Described only as a "strong contributor" who has been "involved in" cache coherence modeling discussions. L3 is a relatively junior level, and the language is participatory rather than ownership-oriented (no indication they lead the effort, are the sole expert, or have scope beyond one workstream on one project). This does not meet the bar for organizational criticality. - NYX-013 (L3, compa-ratio 0.77): Also L3, described as a "strong analog designer" who has been "picking up more responsibility" including "some layout review" on the PMIC team. This signals a developing contributor gaining scope, not yet an owner of a critical function or a scarce specialist whose departure would materially harm the org. None of the three have evidence of: managing people, owning a program/product area end-to-end, being a sole subject-matter expert, or holding scope beyond a single contributor-level workstream. Compa-ratio severity (e.g., NYX-001's 0.43) is explicitly not the basis for criticality per instructions, and the role evidence for all three points to junior/developing-contributor scope rather than genuine organizational criticality. Recommend addressing pay compression through standard means but do not flag any as retention-critical based on the evidence provided.
